Kursleiterin DaF/DaZ, Niveau B2.1: naturalness, level, didactics, scene plausibility

method: We read every German string of the unit again: the start (Folge, gist item), the LS1 Reisebedingungen with inputItems, pool, reserve and micro-output, the LS2 dialogue (14 lines, both scenes) with items, pool, reserve, micro-output and Aussprache, the LS3 table, pool, reserve and cloze, the LS4 texts t1-t5, both exam blocks and strategy cards, the LS5 task (situation, Planungsblatt, persona, opening line, hint words, 11 model turns), the LS6 task (ad, booking confirmation, Leitpunkte, checklist, model text), all endLines, the check items and proofs, the Rückschau, Porträt, Redemittel, story and facts, plus the u04 lexicon entries the validator names. We solved all 91 authored items blind (26 fill_blank, 22 multiple_choice, 14 cloze, 13 sentence_building, 11 error_correction, 4 richtig_falsch, 1 dictation) from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line, permuted every sentence-building item by hand and recorded every key position. The exam blocks and Aufgaben were checked against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/tb2.json (sb1, hv3, sa, m3) with the validator's own wordCount; grammar against grammar-spine.json and b2.1/rule-cards.json; lexis against level-profiles.json (b2.1: newPerUnit 60-70); can-dos against registries/cando/b2.json; voices against casts/b2.json and casts/series.json. We traced the runtime paths earlier findings depend on (ItemView.jsx choiceSet, content.js dictationItems, speakingAI.mjs normalizeSpeakingTask / buildCoursePartnerPrompt). For the three r1 class rules we rebuilt the r1 defects in a scratch copy outside the repo (all 26 non-exam three-option keys at options[0]; ls1-p08 without „Mangelhaft war leider die Unterbringung.“) and validated it. The rule-smith changed the validator four times while we reviewed, so we record the sequence: 19:45 UTC ITM-09 blocked ls2-p06/ls2-p07 with two ungrammatical orders („Wir bitten um einen Preisnachlass Sie.“, „Wir wenden andernfalls uns an die Verbraucherzentrale.“), which disappeared after orders.mjs changed at 19:47; about 19:59 ITM-01 (i04, p05, ls2-p05) and the new non-exam ITM-03 (check 1/3/1) reported blockers; from 20:01 both are advisory or silent. Final run on the unit (20:01 UTC): FAIL, 33 pass, 1 fail (LEX-07, 5 blockers, all in b2.1/lexicon.json entries of u03 and u09), 2 warn (LEX-02 ratchet 67; ITM-03 1 advisory), 4 skipped at unit scope. check.mjs: 0 errors. Scratch copy: ITM-09 FAIL on the ls1-p08 defect (the rule now exists); ITM-03 only 7 advisories for 26 keys at options[0]; ALL-02 PASS. There was no network in this session; the facts were checked from knowledge of the BGB text.
verdict: Not exitable in round 3: 1 BLOCKER, 2 MAJOR, 8 MINOR. The unit side is in good shape. All 91 keys are correct, the four Teile are template-exact and original, and 25 of the 27 earlier findings are fixed or no longer apply to the unit. The r2 regressions are all closed: 714 € = 30 % of 2.380 €, one voice for Blauwelle's Kundenservice, 263 SB1 words, short dictation sources, a du-persona that carries the Planungsblatt, and the two idioms. The only BLOCKER (F01) is not a u04 defect: LEX-07 fails on five b2.1 lexicon entries of u03 and u09, so validate.mjs on this unit is red until the lexicon owner re-allocates them. The gate-hole MAJOR (F02) is narrower than in r2, because the ITM-09 Mittelfeld rule now exists and catches the r1 defect. Non-exam key balance, however, is only advisory until the player owner decides on a seeded shuffle, and ALL-02 is unchanged. The one new unit MAJOR (F03) comes from our own r2 F08 fix: the meaning cue of ls1-r02 now also admits Geschäftsbedingungen, Vertragsbedingungen and AGB. Among the minors, four are unit edits: an open gap (F04), the LS3 endLine word order in the unit that teaches it (F05), one weak distractor set (F06) and small idioms (F07). F08 is a coherence point shared with the lexicon, and F09-F11 are carried class or level items.

findings.problem: validate.mjs on this unit ends with FAIL (5 blockers), and all five are in the shared level lexicon, not in u04. The root cause is the allocation, not the wording. The lemma itself is the unlicensed construction, so no example sentence for these entries can pass. hinsichtlich and bezüglich are allocated to b2.1-u03, but grammar-spine.json licenses g.praep-genitiv-formell only as a chunk from b2.1-u04 and productively from b2.2-u11. bezüglich is even marked productive. infolgedessen, folglich and hingegen are allocated to b2.1-u09 (two of them productive), while g.konsekutiv-adversativ enters at b2.2-u09 with no chunkFrom. As long as LEX-07 is red, u04, which is at stage T, cannot have a green gate set (BLUEPRINT §10.6), even though nothing in u04 needs to change. By §9.4 content this is a level breach (MAJOR). It is logged as BLOCKER because the gate treats the file as invalid.
findings.fix: No u04 change. Lexicon owner, together with the curriculum owner, picks one of two routes. (a) Re-allocate: lx.hinsichtlich and lx.bezueglich to b2.1-u04 or later as receptive chunk entries, and lx.infolgedessen, lx.folglich and lx.hingegen to b2.2-u09. (b) Change the spine: set g.praep-genitiv-formell chunkFrom to b2.1-u03, and give g.konsekutiv-adversativ a chunkFrom of b2.1-u09 with the three lemmas receptive. Then re-run node scripts/course-v2/validate.mjs b2.1.

findings.quote: „Lesen Sie vor der Buchung die ___. (die Regeln, die zum Reisevertrag gehören)“ → accepted: [„Reisebedingungen“]
findings.problem: The meaning cue we proposed in r2 F08 fits more than one noun. „Lesen Sie vor der Buchung die Geschäftsbedingungen / Vertragsbedingungen / AGB.“ is correct German and matches the definition: „die Regeln, die zum Reisevertrag gehören“ is literally what Vertragsbedingungen means, and „AGB“ is the everyday word. The item sits in the plateau, mehr-ueben and repair banks, where the Blauwelle text is not on screen, so Geschäftsbedingungen/AGB is arguably the most likely learner answer. It is graded WRONG. A defensible second answer that is not accepted is a MAJOR under §9.4. ITM-01 cannot see this, because any bracket counts as a cue.
findings.fix: Tie the cue to the travel domain and the text word, e.g. „Lesen Sie vor der Buchung die ___. (die Bedingungen für Ihre Reise, ein Wort: Reise…)“, or „Lesen Sie vor der Buchung die Rei______________.“ (first letters). Add a stem that excludes the general terms: „Nicht die AGB des Onlineshops, sondern die ___ des Veranstalters.“ Alternatively keep the cue and accept „Geschäftsbedingungen“, „Vertragsbedingungen“ and „AGB“ with acceptedWhy, and turn the item into a choice item if the lemma drill matters.

findings.quote: „Eine Leistung fällt aus. Dann erhalten Sie nach Möglichkeit eine gleichwertige ___.“ → accepted: [„Ersatzleistung“]
findings.problem: The stem copies the Abschnitt-2 sentence almost word for word, so the item tests finding a matching string rather than understanding. The open gap also admits correct answers that are not accepted. „eine gleichwertige Alternative“ shows full understanding, and „eine gleichwertige Leistung“ even uses a word from Abschnitt 2. Both are graded WRONG. For a moment at 19:59 UTC, ITM-01 flagged this as an open noun gap without a German cue. From 20:01 it is silent. The item sits directly under the text, so the risk is small, which is why we log it as MINOR.
findings.fix: Paraphrase the stem and cue the word: „Ein Ausflug fällt aus. Was bekommen Sie nach Abschnitt 2 zuerst? Eine gleichwertige ___. (Nomen aus dem Text, beginnt mit „Er“)“. Or accept „Alternative“ and „Leistung“ with acceptedWhy.

findings.quote: „Sie können jetzt sagen, was hätte anders sein müssen – höflich und bestimmt.“
findings.problem: In the standard language the finite auxiliary stands directly before the two infinitives, after the predicative: „…, was anders hätte sein müssen“. „was hätte anders sein müssen“ (Zwischenstellung) is colloquial or regional. It appears on the LS3 win screen, directly after a rule table and card that teach „hätte vor den beiden Infinitiven“.
findings.fix: „Sie können jetzt sagen, was anders hätte sein müssen – höflich und bestimmt.“

findings.quote: „Welcher Satz bedeutet: Wir sind pünktlich gekommen?“ — „Ohne dein Handy wären wir zu spät gekommen.“ (key) · „Wir sind zu spät gekommen.“ · „Wir kommen heute zu spät.“
findings.problem: Both distractors plainly say „late“ in the indicative, and only the key is in the Konjunktiv. A learner who does not understand the irreal past can still find the answer as the odd one out. The item is meant to test the meaning of wären … gekommen (weak distractors, criterion A).
findings.fix: Use distractors that also use Konjunktiv II but mean „late“, e.g. „Mit deinem Handy wären wir pünktlich gekommen.“ and „Ohne dein Handy wären wir pünktlich gekommen.“ Keep the key.

findings.quote: „vom 12. bis 19. Oktober habe ich bei Ihnen eine Pauschalreise gemacht. … Neben unserem Zimmer …“ · „schicken Sie uns diese bitte als E-Mail“
findings.problem: „bei Ihnen eine Pauschalreise gemacht“ is colloquial for a formal complaint; one books a trip with a company („gebucht“). The model then moves from ich to wir („unserem Zimmer“, „um uns gekümmert“) without ever introducing the second traveller. The booking is for 2 Reisende, and the 714 € covers both. In t4, „als E-Mail“ is less idiomatic than „per E-Mail“.
